correctness.rationale: The nested-event representation X_(1)=1_{K=0}, X_(2)=1_{K<=1}, K~Bin(n,q), yields R_n=a(1-b)/[b(1-a)] exactly, with a=(1-q)^n and b=a+nq(1-q)^(n-1). Both fixed-n boundary values vanish. Under nq->c>0 the limiting squared correlation is F(c)=(exp(c)-1-c)/[(1+c)(exp(c)-1)]. The uniform escape bounds R<=1/(1+nq) for nq->infinity and R<=c/(2-c) for c=nq->0 exclude maximizing sequences at either boundary. Differentiation gives F' sign equal to 1+c+c^2-exp(c), whose unique positive zero is established from the change of sign of its second derivative; compactness and comparison at q=c*/n force every optimizer to that limit. Independent differentiation and finite maximization n=2,3,5,10,100,1000 corroborate localization, not an infinite proof.

final_claim: For iid Bernoulli samples, maximizing ordinary Pearson correlation of the first two increasing order statistics over p in (0,1) yields n(1-p_n)->c*, where c*>0 uniquely solves exp(c*)=1+c*+c*^2, and C_n->sqrt(c*)/(1+c*)=0.479412669832... for every choice of finite maximizers.
limitations: iid Bernoulli parent only, n>=2, first two increasing ranks, ordinary Pearson correlation; no finite-n uniqueness or second-order expansion.
